$comment: One table of malformed and well-formed calls, driven through BOTH validators: tests/unit/test_validation.py and packages/server-node/test/validation.test.mjs read this file and assert the same verdict and the same sentence. The same pattern as value-encoding.json, and for the same reason — two hand-written copies of a rule are two rules. `error` is the exact message the call must be refused with, sourced from contract/tools.json -> errors; `error: null` means the call must be accepted. Nothing here touches an OPC UA server: these are checks on the request, made before a session is reached.

cases.$comment: additionalProperties (#114). A misspelled *optional* argument used to be accepted and silently change behaviour — the call browsed with the default node class and returned a plausible wrong answer. The refusal names the tool's real arguments, because 'no such argument' without the list is a riddle to a model that has just guessed one.
cases.name: a misspelled optional argument
cases.error: browse_opcua_nodes has no argument node_clas. It accepts: node_id, browse_path, depth, node_class, name_filter, include_values, max_nodes.

cases.name: an argument from another tool
cases.error: read_opcua_nodes has no argument depth. It accepts: node_ids.

cases.name: an unknown key inside a write entry
cases.error: write_opcua_nodes has no argument nodes[0].units. It accepts: node_id, value, data_type.

cases.name: a tool that takes no arguments, given one
cases.error: get_server_status has no argument verbose. It accepts: no arguments.

cases.name: a tool that takes no arguments, given none

cases.$comment: enum (#114). An unknown node class used to match nothing and come back as an empty list, which is indistinguishable from a subtree that really is empty — the quiet wrong answer this project refuses to give.

cases.$comment: minimum (#114). A negative is never meaningful for any numeric argument here and used to be silently clamped, which is how a caller computing an offset wrongly gets a plausible answer and never finds out. The ceilings stay clamps: they are documented caps on how much work one call may ask for, and the result says when one was hit.
